primary_question: Does a small physically contact-gated impulse bootstrap improve early learning compared with goal plus potential alone, with identical architecture, seeds and compute?
proposed_stack: pinned RocketSim C++ + audited GigaLearn-derived native collector + LibTorch PPO; full-stack benchmark gate before final selection

network.initialization: fresh random; no old bot weights

physics.contract_status: must pass native and deployment clock parity gates

resource_admission_targets.note: Targets to measure and enforce after integration; not claims of measured GTX 1650 consumption

opponents.pilot: current self-play plus a small frozen random-initialization checkpoint pool; assignments only on episode resets
opponents.later: historical snapshots and verified compatible fixed bots, with fresh-seed independent evaluation

gates: GAE terminal/timeout/tail and per-row bootstrap tests
complete rollout used exactly once as declared
old-policy opponent rows excluded from learner loss/count
fixed opponent native versus published inference action agreement

synthetic model examples/s equals end-to-end SPS
high reward or contact drill success proves match strength
unrun RLBot deployment or RewardServer integration works
